q-7567: Correct answer: C. Carrying such a passenger on a two-wheeled motorcycle is prohibited — they do not keep their balance and can cause the vehicle to fall over by their behaviour. Only carrying them in a sidecar is permitted.
q-7568: Correct answer: B. An intoxicated passenger may be carried on a motorcycle only in a sidecar, where they do not affect the vehicle's balance. On the pillion behind the rider such carriage is prohibited regardless of speed.
q-7596: Correct answer: B. Category AM entitles you to drive a moped and a light quadricycle, not every quadricycle. A motorcycle requires category A1, A2 or A, depending on its power and engine capacity.
q-7621: Correct answer: A. The registration document confirms that the trailer has been registered and admitted to traffic on public roads. It certifies neither its current technical state nor that it may be coupled to any vehicle.
q-7625: Correct answer: B. Category T entitles you to drive an agricultural tractor and a slow-moving vehicle, also with trailers. A lorry requires category C, and a light motor vehicle of small unladen mass — category B1.
q-7626: Correct answer: A. Category T covers an agricultural tractor and a slow-moving vehicle together with trailers, including two. A ballast tractor belongs to another group of motor vehicles, and a motorcycle requires category A1, A2 or A.
q-7665: Correct answer: B. The total driving time in two consecutive weeks may not exceed 90 hours. The limit applies regardless of the terms of the employment contract and is meant to prevent tiredness, which lengthens the driver's reaction time.
q-7666: Correct answer: C. Compensatory rest for a reduced week is taken in one go, in full, attached to another rest period. Splitting this compensation into parts is not allowed, because it would not ensure full recovery.
q-7667: Correct answer: B. The driver must have with them the records of their activity for the current day and the previous 28 days and show them during a roadside check. They include record sheets, manual entries and tachograph printouts.
q-7668: Correct answer: B. A regular weekly rest lasts 45 hours, so after reducing it to 24 hours the missing 21 hours must be taken as compensatory rest. It is taken in one go, attached to another rest period.
q-7726: Correct answer: C. A driver may use a reduced daily rest period at most three times between two weekly rest periods. The other daily rests in that interval must be of the full, regular length.
q-7727: Correct answer: B. A regular weekly rest period lasts at least 45 hours. A shorter, reduced weekly rest is allowed only exceptionally and requires the missing time to be taken later.
q-7728: Correct answer: A. Supervising unloading is a work activity that is not driving, so the tachograph switch is set to "other work". A period of availability is recorded when the driver is only waiting and performing no tasks.
q-7764: Correct answer: C. On a regular service the bus driver must have the timetable with them — it is used to check the route, the stops and the times of the run. The other certificates listed do not have to be carried in the vehicle.
q-7850: Correct answer: A. A tachograph records driving time, other work, periods of availability and breaks and rest, including the driver's daily rest. Engine revs and the mass of the load are not recorded on the record sheet.
q-7851: Correct answer: C. Breaks from work and daily rest are recorded by the tachograph under the symbol marked C in the material. It is reserved for time in which the driver performs no tasks and freely disposes of their time.
q-8813: Correct answer: B. Uninterrupted driving may last at most four and a half hours, and four hours have passed since 6.00. So 30 minutes remain before the permitted driving time is used up, after which a break must be taken.
q-8817: Correct answer: C. Whether a tachograph must be used is decided by the sum of the maximum permissible masses of the vehicle and the trailer: 2,800 kg and 750 kg give 3,550 kg, that is, more than 3.5 t. The vehicles of 3,450 kg and 2,800 kg alone do not exceed that threshold.
q-10793: Correct answer: A. A journey by an oversize vehicle is allowed only on the basis of a permit of the appropriate category, so the document must be in the vehicle while driving. The driver shows it at the request of persons authorised to carry out checks.
q-10800: Correct answer: A. The permit specifies, among other things, the route, the permitted vehicle parameters, the time of the journey and the manner of piloting, and the driver must comply with all of them. Whether the load is divisible is of no significance here.
q-10802: Correct answer: A. Exceeding a height of 4 m makes the combination an oversize vehicle, and its journey requires a permit of the appropriate category. This follows from clearance limits under flyovers, bridges and overhead lines; the divisibility of the load does not release you from the duty.
q-10804: Correct answer: A. An actual total mass of 50 tonnes or more exceeds the values permitted for ordinary traffic, so the journey takes place solely on the basis of a permit of the appropriate category. The duty applies to all roads, not only national ones.
q-10808: Correct answer: B. A child under 3 may be carried in a car only when the vehicle has seat belts and the child is placed in a child seat or another restraint matched to its height and weight.
q-10809: Correct answer: A. Without seat belts and a child seat or another restraint, carrying a child under three is prohibited. Holding the child in your arms is no substitute for a child seat — in a collision an adult is unable to hold on to it.
q-10818: Correct answer: C. The receipt for a retained national driving licence allows you to drive a vehicle for only 24 hours from the moment of retention. After that time, driving on means driving without the required entitlement.
q-10825: Correct answer: B. A foreign driving licence is retained against a receipt when a car has been carrying 3 people more than the registration document indicates. A smaller excess of passengers is punished but does not result in the document being retained.
q-10826: Correct answer: C. The checking authority verifies the vehicle's admission to traffic and its third-party insurance in the registers, so those documents need not be carried. A driver whose licence carries an alcohol-interlock requirement must, however, have with them confirmation of its calibration.
q-10827: Correct answer: A. If the registration document or the temporary permit has been retained, the driver carries the receipt for that retention and shows it for a check. The registration document itself and the third-party policy need not be carried.
q-10828: Correct answer: C. Driving entitlements issued in Poland are visible in the central register, so a national driving licence need not be carried or shown. This does not, however, release you from the duty to actually hold valid entitlements.
q-10832: Correct answer: A. An inspection carried out by an unauthorised unit is invalid, so the vehicle is treated as not admitted to traffic and the registration document is subject to retention. A faulty number-plate light is a minor fault, and the document need not be carried anyway.
q-10834: Correct answer: B. A national driving licence need not be carried, because the entitlement is visible in the register. If, however, the driver relies on another document entitling them to drive, for example one issued abroad, they must have it with them and show it.
q-10835: Correct answer: A. When the driving licence has been retained, the driver drives on the basis of the receipt and must have it with them for the whole of its validity. The driving licence itself and proof of payment of the third-party premium need not be carried.
q-10836: Correct answer: C. Apart from the documents under the road traffic rules, the driver must carry those required by other acts, for example concerning road haulage or the carriage of dangerous goods. A national driving licence and proof of payment of the third-party premium need not be carried.
q-10838: Correct answer: A. The exemption from carrying the document concerns only a national driving licence visible in the Polish register. A driver relying on an entitlement issued elsewhere must have that document with them and show it on request.
q-10839: Correct answer: B. During a test drive the vehicle is not registered under the ordinary rules, so the driver must carry the document admitting it to traffic, that is, the professional registration document together with the form. A national driving licence need not be shown.
q-10841: Correct answer: C. A driver whose entitlement has been restricted to vehicles with an alcohol interlock must carry a certificate of a positive technical check of that interlock. A national driving licence or the registration document need not be shown.
q-10842: Correct answer: A. A driver who holds a driving licence issued in Poland does not have to carry it — the person checking verifies their entitlements in the central register. Not having the document on you therefore carries no penalty by itself.
q-10843: Correct answer: B. A national driving licence and the registration document of a Polish vehicle need not be carried, because the data are checked in the registers. What must be carried is the document on the calibration of the alcohol interlock, if the duty to use one follows from the driving licence.
q-10844: Correct answer: A. A police officer may establish the driver's identity from data in the state registers, including the identity-card register. They may not, however, demand a national driving licence or the third-party policy of a Polish vehicle, because they check that information electronically.
q-10999: Correct answer: C. When the registration document has been retained, its role is played by the receipt, and that is what must be in the vehicle for the time it entitles you to drive. The driver need not carry a national driving licence or third-party confirmation — the data are in the registers.
q-11029: Correct answer: A. A motorcycle's admission to traffic is confirmed by the registration document and, before it is issued, by the temporary permit. The driving licence concerns the rider's entitlements, and the identity card solely the person's identity.
q-11037: Correct answer: C. A vehicle's admission to traffic is confirmed by the registration document and, until it is issued, by the temporary permit. The vehicle card documents its history, and a report from the register is only information about the data.
q-11041: Correct answer: B. The registration document of a vehicle registered in Poland and a technical inspection certificate need not be carried, because those data are in the registers. If, however, the trailer's document has been retained, the driver must have the receipt for the time it entitles them to drive.
q-11042: Correct answer: A. The owner is to collect the registration decision and the registration document within 30 days of the day the registration application was submitted. The period runs from the application, not from the vehicle's first outing on the road.
q-11047: Correct answer: A. The entitlement to drive an agricultural tractor is confirmed by a category T driving licence issued in Poland. The vehicle card concerns the vehicle itself, and an image of the document in an app does not replace holding the required entitlements.
q-11059: Correct answer: A. The entitlement to ride a motorcycle is confirmed by a valid driving licence of the appropriate category, matched to the type of motorcycle. A temporary permit concerns the vehicle's admission to traffic, not the rider's entitlements.
q-11060: Correct answer: B. Category A1 covers light motorcycles and three-wheeled motorcycles with a power not exceeding 15 kW. A slow-moving vehicle and a quadricycle require other entitlements and do not fall within the scope of this category.
q-11061: Correct answer: C. Category A1 includes the entitlements of category AM, so it allows you to drive a moped and a light quadricycle. A motorcycle with a power of up to 45 kW requires category A2, and a slow-moving vehicle other entitlements.
q-11070: Correct answer: A. Destruction of a driving licence to the point of illegibility is reported to the starosta within 30 days of the event. The report is the basis for issuing a duplicate of the document.
q-11073: Correct answer: A. The driving licence is retained for 3 months when the driver has exceeded the permitted speed by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area. Smaller excesses, such as 45 or 40 km/h, have no such effect, although they remain an offence.
q-11075: Correct answer: A. Retention of the driving licence for 3 months follows exceeding the permitted speed by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area. With a limit of 40 km/h, that threshold is crossed only by driving faster than 90 km/h.
q-11077: Correct answer: A. For the driving licence to be retained for 3 months, the permitted speed must be exceeded by more than 50 km/h in a built-up area. In a 30 km/h zone that means driving faster than 80 km/h.
q-11080: Correct answer: A. The driving licence is also retained for 3 months when the driver carries more people than the number of seats entered in the registration document. Exceeding the speed limit outside a built-up area has no such effect.
q-11085: Correct answer: C. The decision to retain the driving licence takes away the right to drive, not just the document itself, so for the whole of that period riding a motorcycle is prohibited. Breaking the ban results in the retention period being extended.
q-11520: Correct answer: C. As a rule a lorry may tow one trailer, so a combination with two trailers is allowed only on the basis of a permit. It makes no difference whether the trailers are loaded or empty.
q-14059: Correct answer: B. An application to register a motorcycle acquired in Poland is submitted to the starosta's office within 30 days of its acquisition. Exceeding that deadline risks a financial penalty, so it is better to deal with the formalities at once.
q-14061: Correct answer: C. Driving a motor vehicle despite a driving-licence retention extended to 6 months results in the driving entitlement being withdrawn for 5 years from the day that event is established. Further extension of the retention period is then no longer applied.
q-4043: Correct answer: B. The parking brake holds the wheels by spring force, so neither switching off the car nor setting the reverser will release it. For towing, the release devices are unhooked mechanically or electrically, and the car must first be secured against rolling away.
q-4065: Correct answer: B. Getting on and off takes place only at stops, prepared for passengers' safe access. Away from a stop a passenger steps straight onto the carriageway between moving vehicles, and their haste changes nothing here.
q-4067: Correct answer: B. The exchange of passengers takes place at stops, because only there is access to the vehicle prepared and other drivers expect pedestrians. Stopping elsewhere exposes those getting off to contact with vehicle traffic.
q-4075: Correct answer: C. When the vehicle is immobilised for a long time, letting the passengers out is permitted, but only where they can get off safely and it will not endanger traffic on the road. The choice of place is decided by safety, not by convenience or passengers' requests.
q-4077: Correct answer: B. Before the tram driver steps onto the carriageway, the car must be immobilised and secured, and leaving the cab is preceded by checking that nothing is approaching. Switching off the converter or the lights does not make this manoeuvre safe.
q-4079: Correct answer: B. The car's metal body conducts the charge along its shell, so the interior remains safe and the journey can continue. Stopping the set and letting people out into the open would increase the danger.
q-4089: Correct answer: B. The electrodynamic brake can be metered smoothly, so it serves for shedding speed. At very low speed its effectiveness fades, so stopping and holding the car is taken over by the parking brake. The track brake is an emergency brake and stops abruptly.
q-4092: Correct answer: A. Carrying passengers in a car with faulty doors is not permitted, because open doors risk a person falling out onto the track. Once everyone has been asked to leave, the car returns to the depot as an empty run. Switching off the traction interlock is prohibited.
q-4099: Correct answer: B. A towed car increases the mass of the set, and its own brakes usually do not work to their full extent, so the braking distance grows clearly. Drive slower, avoid sudden manoeuvres and keep a greater distance.
q-4109: Correct answer: C. The space between the cars is dangerous for passengers, so the absence of a guard is permitted only when the coupling bears a marking prohibiting stepping between the cars. Without such a marking, driving is not allowed.
q-4119: Correct answer: B. Smooth but decisive braking lets the car be stopped precisely at the platform without knocking standing passengers over. Harsh braking and simultaneous use of all the brakes are kept for emergencies.
q-4138: Correct answer: B. The tram driver may move off, but only with special care: they constantly watch the people at the edge of the platform and are ready to stop the car immediately. Running late against the timetable does not justify the risk.
q-4142: Correct answer: A. Before the doors are opened, the tram driver checks in the right exterior mirror whether the vehicles on the carriageway have stopped — those getting off may end up in their path. The doors are opened only once the exit is safe.
q-6474: Correct answer: C. Carrying a child under seven on a motorcycle is permitted only at a clearly reduced speed, so of the values given only the lowest falls within it. The other speeds are too high.
q-6477: Correct answer: A. The lower of the values always applies: the limit arising from the sign shown in the material and the reduced limit when carrying a child under seven. Here 20 km/h is binding.
q-6488: Correct answer: C. Carrying a child under seven on a moped is permitted only at a clearly reduced speed, so of the values given only the lowest falls within it. The other speeds are too high.
q-6492: Correct answer: A. The lower of the values is always binding: the limit arising from the sign shown in the material and the reduced limit in force when carrying a child under seven. Here 20 km/h is permitted.
q-6562: Correct answer: B. A passenger affects the balance of a two-wheeler, so before the ride they must be told how to get on, where to keep their feet and hands and to lean together with the motorcycle. The extra load calls rather for firmer suspension and correct tyre pressure.
q-6566: Correct answer: B. A passenger changes the balance of a moped, so before the ride they must be told how to get on, where to rest their feet and hands and that they lean together with the vehicle. Lowering tyre pressure and softening the suspension only worsen the handling.
q-6568: Correct answer: C. If the motorcycle has no factory-fitted seat belts, both the rider and the passenger carried must wear a protective helmet — the one in the sidecar too. Without a helmet, carrying a person is not permitted, regardless of distance and speed.
q-6569: Correct answer: A. A child is carried in a protective helmet, on the passenger seat intended for it and only when its feet reach the footrests. A two-seat motorcycle may carry one such person, so a place on the fuel tank or between two people is ruled out.
q-6571: Correct answer: B. A combination of a motorcycle and a trailer may be no longer than 4 m. A longer combination would be hard to control when turning and turning round, and with the mass of the towing vehicle also unstable.
q-6573: Correct answer: C. A trailer towed by a motorcycle has no separate number — the number plate transferred from the motorcycle is placed at its rear, because the vehicle's own plate is then hidden. A flag does not replace registration marking.
q-6575: Correct answer: B. The load must be fastened so that it can neither shift nor fall off, because a shift of weight immediately upsets the balance of a two-wheeler. The lights and the number plate must not be covered either.
q-6577: Correct answer: C. On a moped both the rider and the passenger must wear a protective helmet — without exception. Even a fall at low speed ends with the head striking the surface, and a helmet is the only real protection in such a situation.
q-6578: Correct answer: C. A moped passenger may not ride without a protective helmet; the duty to wear one covers them just as it does the rider. Talking to the rider or using their own phone is not prohibited for a passenger.
q-6579: Correct answer: B. A carried load is secured against shifting and falling off, because even a small shift of mass changes the motorcycle's behaviour in a bend and under braking. Covering the number plate and the lights is prohibited.
q-6580: Correct answer: A. A load is fastened above all so as not to impair the motorcycle's stability — low, close to the vehicle's axis and symmetrically. Reaching into the luggage while riding is not acceptable, and aerodynamics is of secondary importance here.
q-6581: Correct answer: A. A motorcycle is towed only on a flexible connection that can be released quickly — if either vehicle loses balance, the rope must let go at once. A rigid connection between two two-wheelers is not permitted.
q-6582: Correct answer: C. Towing a motorcycle is allowed, but only on a flexible connection that can easily be released. The rider of the towed two-wheeler must be able to free themselves immediately when they begin to lose balance.
q-6588: Correct answer: B. A combination of a moped and a trailer may be at most 4 m long. With so light a towing vehicle, a longer trailer would begin to dictate the line of travel, especially under braking and in bends.
q-6589: Correct answer: A. With so light a vehicle every badly placed weight changes its behaviour, so the load is fastened low and symmetrically so as not to impair the moped's stability. Access to the luggage while riding and aerodynamics are irrelevant here.
q-6648: Correct answer: B. The sign shown in the material marks an area in which the permitted speed for all vehicles is 20 km/h. The restriction also applies to an agricultural tractor with a trailer and lasts until the cancelling sign.
q-6651: Correct answer: A. Carrying people in a trailer towed by an agricultural tractor is permitted only at a speed not exceeding 20 km/h. The restriction follows from the lack of protection for the passengers and applies regardless of the general limit on the road.
q-6652: Correct answer: C. In a trailer towed by an agricultural tractor a work crew of at most 5 people may be carried. The carriage must take place at a limited speed, and the people may not ride on the load or outside the designated places.
q-6653: Correct answer: C. People carrying out loading work may ride standing in the trailer if they hold on to the handholds and their number is within the permitted limit. A crew of seven exceeds that limit, and the carriage of escorts with the load does not concern an agricultural tractor's trailer.
q-6654: Correct answer: C. The sign prohibits entry to vehicles whose actual total mass exceeds the value given on it, that is, 2.5 t. With a tractor and trailer, the mass of the whole combination together with its load counts, not the weight of the goods carried alone.
q-6656: Correct answer: A. If the dimensions of the combination do not allow turning from the right edge of the carriageway, the manoeuvre may be started from another position, taking special care. This does not, however, give the right to drive onto the pavement or cross a solid line.
q-6657: Correct answer: C. Towing on a flexible connection is permitted when the towed vehicle has working brakes and the connection can easily be released. A vehicle with a faulty braking system may not be towed on a rope, and towing a combination with a trailer is prohibited.
q-6663: Correct answer: B. A trailer must be equipped with side reflectors, thanks to which it is visible from the side, especially after dark at junctions. Towing a trailer lacking the required equipment is not allowed regardless of its length.
q-6665: Correct answer: A. In a two-line system the coupling and the supply line, which brings compressed air to the trailer's reservoir, are marked in red. Yellow is assigned to the control line, which is meant to prevent the two couplings being mixed up when coupling.
q-6666: Correct answer: B. The control line, which passes to the trailer the signal that the brake in the tractor has been applied, is marked in yellow. Red is reserved for the supply line, so the colours allow the couplings to be connected correctly.
q-6667: Correct answer: A. A drop in pressure in the supply line causes the trailer to brake automatically with the air stored in its reservoir. As a result a trailer that breaks away from the tractor stops by itself instead of rolling on out of control.
q-6669: Correct answer: C. A trailer's rear reflectors are triangular, which distinguishes it from a motor vehicle and lets you recognise from afar that a combination of vehicles is ahead. Round and rectangular reflectors are used elsewhere on the vehicle.
q-6671: Correct answer: B. A combination with an agricultural tractor moves slowly, so at the rear it must have the triangular distinguishing plate, visible to those approaching from behind. The plate is placed on the last vehicle of the combination, that is, on the trailer.
q-6680: Correct answer: B. The mirrors are set so that on both sides you can see the road behind the combination, with the edge of the trailer visible only at the edge of the mirror as a reference point. Too large a piece of your own vehicle in the mirror enlarges the blind spot.
q-6682: Correct answer: B. The pneumatic system is designed so that the trailer's brakes act slightly earlier than the tractor's. Thanks to this the combination stays stretched out and the trailer does not push against the tractor, which would risk the vehicles jack-knifing.
q-6683: Correct answer: C. The lower the gear, the greater the engine resistance passed to the wheels, so engine braking is more effective; the gear is chosen so as not to exceed the permitted revs. A pressed clutch cuts off that effect completely.
q-6684: Correct answer: A. The gear is chosen before the climb, because changing down on a steep ascent with a heavy trailer causes loss of speed, and even stopping and the combination rolling back. The gear chosen should allow a steady speed to be held right to the top.
q-6686: Correct answer: A. Drive to both axles spreads the driving force over more wheels, so on a slippery surface the wheels spin less and the combination handles more stably. Shifting the load rearwards unloads the driven axle and worsens grip.
q-6687: Correct answer: A. When reversing, you must see the space behind the trailer and at the same time check the path of both vehicles in the mirrors, because the trailer turns the opposite way to the steering wheel and the front of the tractor swings in a wide arc. With limited visibility, the help of another person is used.
q-6688: Correct answer: C. The driver's attention is focused on the road ahead, and the mirrors are checked regularly with short glances, to know who intends to overtake the slow-moving combination. Constant watching of the rear would draw the eyes away from what is happening ahead.
q-6694: Correct answer: A. A loose load is carried in a sealed body with curtains, because material spilling onto the carriageway reduces grip and can strike vehicles behind. A tarpaulin alone on a leaky body will not stop spillage from below.
q-6695: Correct answer: C. The permitted payload may not be exceeded on any road, because an overloaded trailer has a longer braking distance, overloads the axle and the hitch and damages the surface. The type of road does not change this ban.
q-6696: Correct answer: B. A passenger may be carried only on the seat intended for it, if the tractor is fitted with one. Riding on the mudguard, the hitch or another part of the structure risks falling under the wheels and is prohibited.
q-6723: Correct answer: A. No battery charging is signalled by a red light with a battery symbol and pole markings; in the set that is variant A. If it shines with the engine running, the charging system is faulty and driving must be limited.
q-6728: Correct answer: B. A foreign object is left in the wound, because it partly closes the damaged vessels, and pulling it out increases the bleeding. The edges of the wound are packed with a dressing that stabilises the object, and an ambulance is called.
q-6739: Correct answer: C. Beyond the sign shown in the material a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may travel at no more than 80 km/h — that is the limit on an expressway and on a two-way dual carriageway outside a built-up area.
q-6740: Correct answer: C. Outside a built-up area, on the road indicated by the sign in the material, a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may travel at no more than 70 km/h. On an expressway and a dual carriageway the limit is higher.
q-6741: Correct answer: B. In a built-up area a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may not exceed 50 km/h, so driving at 70 km/h is not allowed. The time of day does not change this restriction.
q-6742: Correct answer: A. On an expressway a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may travel at no more than 80 km/h. Speed-limit signs may lower that limit; they never raise it.
q-6743: Correct answer: A. A combination of a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t and a trailer may travel on the road indicated by the sign at no more than 70 km/h. The higher limit applies to motorways and dual-carriageway expressways.
q-6751: Correct answer: C. A lorry together with its load may be no higher than 4 m. Exceeding that height means an oversize vehicle and requires a permit, and also risks striking a flyover or an overhead line.
q-6752: Correct answer: A. A combination of a motor vehicle and a towed trailer may be at most 18.75 m long. A longer combination is an oversize vehicle and may move only on the basis of a permit.
q-6755: Correct answer: C. The actual mass of a trailer towed by a lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may exceed the actual mass of the towing vehicle by at most 40%. A heavier trailer worsens the stability and braking of the combination.
q-6763: Correct answer: C. After four and a half hours of uninterrupted driving the driver is entitled to a break lasting at least 45 minutes. It may be split into two parts: the first lasting at least 15 minutes and the second at least 30 minutes.
q-6832: Correct answer: C. A vehicle carrying dangerous goods is marked with plates placed at the front and the rear, so that they are visible from both directions. Thanks to this, other drivers and the rescue services know at once what load they are dealing with.
q-6845: Correct answer: A. A combination of a bus and a light trailer may travel on a road marked with the sign in the material at no more than 80 km/h. A trailer lengthens the braking distance and worsens stability, so the limit for the combination is no higher than for the bus alone.
q-6850: Correct answer: C. The number of seats in a bus does not affect the permitted speed. On a road marked with the sign in the material, 80 km/h applies, and the raised limit depends solely on meeting the additional technical conditions.
q-6857: Correct answer: B. A combination of a bus and a trailer may be at most 18.75 m long. A longer combination would not fit properly round curves and junctions, so exceeding that value is not permitted.
q-6859: Correct answer: C. The number of people carried may not exceed the value given in the notice stating the permitted number of seated and standing places. Overloading a bus worsens its stability and braking and hinders the evacuation of passengers.
q-6861: Correct answer: B. The stop brake immobilises the bus while passengers get on and off and limits the use of compressed air, because the driver does not have to keep the brake pedal pressed. It serves neither for slowing down in traffic nor for a long stop.
q-6862: Correct answer: C. The stop brake engages automatically when the bus doors are opened and releases when they are closed. Thanks to this the vehicle stands still while passengers get on and off, without the brake pedal being used.
q-6907: Correct answer: A. The duty to fasten belts applies to every seat fitted with them, in a bus too, and does not depend on whether there is another seat in front of the passenger. The backrest of the seat in front does not protect against the effects of harsh braking or a rollover.
q-6908: Correct answer: A. Passengers together with their luggage constitute the vehicle's load, so their combined mass may not exceed the bus's permitted payload. The maximum permissible mass also includes the vehicle's unladen mass, so it is not a measure of the load itself.
q-6909: Correct answer: C. Luggage is carried in the compartments intended for it, where it is secured against shifting. Items left on the seats or in the aisle injure passengers under braking and block the escape route in an accident.
q-6910: Correct answer: B. Luggage with sharp edges is particularly dangerous for passengers, so it must travel in the luggage compartments, separated from the passenger area. Placed in the aisle or under a seat, it shifts under braking and can cause serious injury.
q-6911: Correct answer: C. The driver of a bus carrying passengers may not smoke while driving. It occupies the hands and attention, and the smoke harms the travellers. A hands-free kit and the radio are allowed, provided they do not distract the driver.
q-6912: Correct answer: A. The driver of a bus with passengers may not eat while driving, because it takes a hand off the wheel and attention off the road. Navigation and a CB radio are permitted, provided operating them does not interfere with driving.
q-6913: Correct answer: B. Before moving off, the driver must make sure all the doors are closed, because driving with the doors open risks a passenger falling out. The indicator is switched on only when the manoeuvre requires it, and announcing the stop is not a condition of moving off.
q-6934: Correct answer: B. The bus driver is responsible for the safety of the people carried, and behaviour that hinders driving makes safe driving impossible. Stop the vehicle in a safe place and call the appropriate services instead of driving on.
q-6936: Correct answer: A. In a fire the priority is human life and health, so the driver first stops the vehicle and organises the evacuation, and only then thinks about property. Luggage and the state of the vehicle may never delay leaving the coach.
q-6938: Correct answer: C. Fire in a coach develops very quickly, so you must stop the vehicle immediately, switch off the engine and get the passengers outside. Fighting the fire may be attempted only once the people are already safe.
q-7093: Correct answer: A. A faulty door-closing mechanism means people cannot be carried safely — driving on with passengers is not allowed. The fault is reported and the operator's instructions followed; switching off the traction interlock is not acceptable.
q-7117: Correct answer: C. Before towing, check that the coupling joins both vehicles securely and will not part while moving. The connection parting on the route would mean the damaged car running out of control and an immediate danger.
q-7120: Correct answer: B. A driver who cannot concentrate on driving must stop safely and call the appropriate services. Continuing to drive in such a situation endangers the passengers and other road users.
q-7122: Correct answer: B. When the doors are jammed, passengers are got out immediately through the emergency exits, marked in the vehicle and equipped with hammers for breaking the windows. Waiting for the services to arrive needlessly prolongs the danger.
q-7199: Correct answer: B. Supervising unloading is performing work duties, so this time counts as other work, not as a break or a period of availability. The appropriate mode must be set on the tachograph.
q-7253: Correct answer: C. A passenger carried on a motorcycle must wear a fastened protective helmet, so the rider may not allow them to ride without one. Talking to the rider or on the phone is not prohibited for a passenger.
q-7510: Correct answer: B. Motorcycles are joined with a flexible connection that can be released instantly. When one of the riders loses balance, the other vehicle must not be pulled along by them — that is why quick release is a condition of safety.
q-7511: Correct answer: A. A trailer towed by a motorcycle may not weigh more than the unladen mass of that motorcycle and in no case more than 100 kg. A heavier trailer would set the two-wheeler swaying and lengthen its braking distance.
q-7520: Correct answer: A. A lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may travel on this road at no more than 80 km/h, even though for cars the limit is higher. The driver always applies the lower value — the one provided for their type of vehicle.
q-7521: Correct answer: B. A speed-limit sign does not lift the limits set for particular types of vehicle. A lorry with a maximum permissible mass above 3.5 t may not go faster than 80 km/h outside a built-up area, so the lower of the two values applies.
